title: Clinical Mastery: Ocular Manifestations of Histiocytosis
summary: Histiocytosis encompasses a group of rare, heterogeneous disorders characterized by the abnormal proliferation and accumulation of histiocytes (macrophages/dendritic cells). In ophthalmology, these systemic diseases frequently present with orbital involvement, proptosis, and eyelid lesions.

sections.title: Definition & Overview
sections.content: Histiocytosis is defined as a clonal or reactive proliferation of dendritic cells or macrophages. Clinical manifestations are categorized by the Histiocyte Society into three main groups: Class L (Langerhans-cell), Class C (Cutaneous/Mucocutaneous), and Class M (Malignant). Ocular involvement is most common in Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis (LCH) and Erdheim-Chester Disease (ECD).

branches: Class M: Histiocytic Sarcoma, Follicular Dendritic Cell Sarcoma

sections.title: Red Flags: When to Biopsy
content: Unilateral proptosis in a pediatric patient
Spontaneous hyphema in an infant (suggests JXG)
'Punched-out' lytic bone lesions on orbital CT
Bilateral orbital masses with scleral thickening
New-onset diabetes insipidus in patient with orbital lesion

sections.title: Management Strategy
content: Step 1: Surgical biopsy for histopathological confirmation (CD1a, CD68, S-100 markers)
Step 2: BRAF V600E mutation testing (Targeted therapy potential)
Step 3: Systemic workup (PET/CT, skeletal survey, endocrine function)
Step 4: LCH: Vinblastine + Prednisone or systemic chemotherapy
Step 5: ECD: BRAF inhibitors (Vemurafenib) or Interferon-alpha
Step 6: Ocular local therapy: Low-dose radiation or intralesional triamcinolone

sections.title: Diagnostic Workup
content: Imaging: MRI Orbit with/without contrast (T1/T2 signal characteristics)
CT Orbit: Best for bone erosion/lytic patterns
Immunohistochemistry: CD1a and Langerin positivity (LCH)
IHC: S-100 and CD68 positivity (Rosai-Dorfman/JXG)
Laboratory: Complete Metabolic Panel, CBC, endocrine profile (ADH/osmolality)

content.explanation: H: Histiocytosis (LCH), A: Age (childhood), N: Nephrogenic Diabetes Insipidus, D: Defects in bone (lytic), S: Skin rash (seborrheic)

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls
content: Always evaluate for Diabetes Insipidus in any patient diagnosed with orbital LCH, as pituitary involvement is common.
In cases of spontaneous pediatric hyphema, suspect Juvenile Xanthogranuloma; iris involvement can lead to secondary glaucoma.
Erdheim-Chester disease is an inflammatory myeloid neoplasm; prioritize cardiological screening as it is a leading cause of mortality.
Rosai-Dorfman disease presents with emperipolesis (phagocytosis of lymphocytes) on histopathology.

sections.title: Recent Advances
sections.content: The identification of MAPK pathway mutations (specifically BRAF V600E) has revolutionized treatment. Targeted therapies like Vemurafenib and Dabrafenib have significantly improved outcomes in refractory ECD and LCH, reducing reliance on traditional systemic chemotherapy.
